The HUD VASH program is an important
partnership between the Department of
Housing and Urban Development and the
Department of Veteran Affairs.
This program is designed specifically to
address the needs of homeless veterans
and their families by focusing on two
things: rental assistance and supportive
services.
The goal is to provide permanent housing
for homeless veterans.
This illustration shows how the program
works.
HUD provides the Norwalk Housing
Authority with HUD VASH vouchers and
funding. The VA identifies homeless
veterans and refers them to the NHA.

guidelines, we will issue a voucher to
subsidize their rent.

ongoing case management and supportive
services to help veterans stabilize.
Congress has supported the HUD VASH
program with yearly funding since 2008
with vouchers awarded based on PHA need
and performance.

meet eligibility requirements, register
our interest to receive vouchers, and
collaborate with the local VA.
For the Norwalk Housing Authority, the
application process began in August
2025, leading to an award of 18 vouchers
in March 2026.

and took effect on August 1st, 2026.

fund. The program is funded fully by HUD
to support the program's launch.
